main_text.head: LIBER PRIMUS CONTRA SCEPTICOS. CAPUT PRIMUM.
main_text.p: ANtiquissimi Philosophi (quos Academici & Sceptici pro se laudare solent) dubitarunt, an ulla rerum cognitio daretur. Heraclitus Ephesius, Gorgias Leontinus, Anaxagoras, Democritus, Empedocles, Parmenides, Xenophanes, Protagoras, Zeno Eleates, ac Nausiphanes consortes Scepticismi fuerunt, aut saltem ad eum accedere visi sunt.

ERRORES, qui absurditatibus proprijs everti creduntur, ut plurimum praesidium in antiquitate inveniunt, quam dum velut scutum aliquod objiciunt, non solum perennant, sed praeter plebejas animas, haut paucos ex ijs quoque, qui supra vulgum sapere videntur, corripiunt ac transversos agunt.

page.notes: The opening word of the second paragraph is a large woodcut initial "E" joined to "RRORES". Ligatures and long-s forms were normalised to plain s. The title lines are set in spaced capitals and italic; the heading is given as a single level-1 division. Printed "Quae" at the foot is the catchword. The page number is not printed.
